question: The speed of a train is 110 kmph. Find the distance covered by the train in 100 seconds.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiply the speed in kmph directly by (5 ÷ 18) to convert it to m/s, then multiply by time to find the distance.

Distance = Speed × Time

Distance = 110 × (5 ÷ 18) × 100 = (550 ÷ 18) × 100

Distance = 27500 ÷ 9 = 3055.555... m

**∴ The correct answer is 3055.56 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of train = 110 kmph

Time = 100 seconds

• Distance = ? 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed in m/s = 110 × (5 ÷ 18)

⇒ Speed = 550 ÷ 18 = 275 ÷ 9 m/s

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = (275 ÷ 9) × 100

⇒ Distance = 27500 ÷ 9

⇒ Distance ≈ 3055.56 m

**∴ The correct answer is 3055.56 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed value by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply the speed value by 18 ÷ 5.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is |S₁ − S₂|. When they move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed

Average Speed is calculated as Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at two different speeds a and b, Average Speed = 2ab ÷ (a + b).
